result.topic_en: Euler applies his third method to the double series q^m (sums of the form ζ(m,1)-type) of orders m+n=8, 9 and 11, expressing them through the simple sums p^n: order 8 is not fully determined, while orders 9 and 11 are determined uniquely.

items.quote: neque ergo haec tertia methodus plenam determinationem suppeditat, cum tamen pro casibus $m+n=5$ et $m+n=7$ esset largita.
items.english: Therefore this third method does not supply a complete determination either, although it had provided one for the cases m+n=5 and m+n=7.

items.quote: Hic ope tertiae methodi omnia determinentur idque vnico modo
items.english: Here, by means of the third method, everything is determined, and that in a unique way.

items.quote: praetermisso ordine decimo obseruo etiam vndecimum perfecte determinari posse
items.english: Passing over the tenth order, I observe that the eleventh can also be perfectly determined.
